message.content:
In Blackjack, an Ace is a “soft” card because it can be counted as either **1** or **11**, depending on which value gives your hand the best chance of winning without busting.  

- If counting the Ace as 11 keeps your total ≤ 21, you’ll usually treat it as 11.  
- If adding 11 would bust you, you’ll treat it as 1.  

If you have two Aces, one will normally be counted as 11 and the other as 1 (so you’re at 12), unless you’re playing a variation where a pair of Aces can be split.  

This flexibility is why hands like “soft 17” (Ace + 6) are treated differently from “hard 17” (no Ace or Ace counted as 1).
